results.title: Artificial intelligence in STEM education: a transdisciplinary ...
results.content: The review focused on peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 that addressed AI applications in STEM education, transdisciplinary approaches to AI integration, and the ethical challenges inherent in AI-driven learning environments. The discussion sections of this paper are structured as follows: the Background and Importance section outlines the evolution of AI in education and underscores the necessity for transdisciplinary collaboration; the Literature Review synthesizes current research and identifies key gaps; the Actionable Strategies for AI-Driven STEM Education section proposes practical frameworks to support inclusive and ethical AI integration; the Implications and Future Directions section discusses policy considerations and emerging research trajectories; and finally, the Conclusion offers closing insights and recommendations to foster engagement, innovation, and ethical practice in AI-powered STEM education. results.title: Artificial intelligence in education: A systematic literature ...
results.content: # Artificial intelligence in education: A systematic literature review. Artificial intelligence (AI) in education (AIED) has evolved into a substantial body of literature with diverse perspectives. In this review paper, we seek insights into three critical questions: (1) What are the primary categories of AI applications explored in the education field? A bibliometric analysis of 2,223 research articles followed by a content analysis of selected 125 papers reveals a comprehensive conceptual structure of the existing literature. The extant AIED research spans a wide spectrum of applications, encompassing those for adaptive learning and personalized tutoring, intelligent assessment and management, profiling and prediction, and emerging products. Research topics delve into both the technical design of education systems and the examination of the adoption, impacts, and challenges associated with AIED. Furthermore, this review highlights the diverse range of theories applied in the AIED literature, the multidisciplinary nature of publication venues, and underexplored research areas.

results.title: From procrastination to engagement? An experimental ...
results.content: An experimental exploration of the effects of an adaptive virtual assistant on self-regulation in online learning. Adaptive assistance can be effective in compensating for self-regulatory skills. Compensatory (behavioural) shifts are moderated by learners’ personality traits. Compared to traditional classroom learning, success in online learning tends to depend more on the learner’s skill to self-regulate. Self-regulation is a complex meta-cognitive skill set that can be acquired. This study explores the effectiveness of a virtual learning assistant in terms of (a) developmental, (b) general compensatory, and (c) differential compensatory effects on learners’ self-regulatory skills in a sample of *N* = 157 online learners using an experimental intervention-control group design. Results indicate that the adaptive assistance did not lead to substantial developmental shifts as captured in learners’ perceived levels of self-regulation. This suggests that the virtual learning assistant has the potential to help online learners effectively compensate for deficits (in contrast to developmental shifts) in self-regulatory skills that might not yet have been developed.
